subject: Every inline Code and HTML node's position, compared with cmark-gfm's own --sourcepos over the CommonMark spec fixture.
purpose:
ZERO ROWS. Every inline Code and HTML position over the CommonMark spec fixture now agrees with cmark-gfm, and this gate's job from here is to keep it that way: a row APPEARING fails it just as a row clearing does.

It read twelve at the baseline, all one cause. Our side reported a span that crossed a line ending as though it had not: the start always agreed, and the end named a column on the START line, usually past the end of it. adjust_subj_node_newlines is the only code that walks a consumed span's line endings and it was gated behind MARKDOWN_CORE_OPT_SOURCEPOS, which nothing in the tree ever set. 0a.6 un-gated it and all twelve cleared, with none appearing.

§4.2.3 predicted one survivor, spec example 200, on the content-offset-as-column class. THAT PREDICTION WAS WRONG in both directions: example 200 agreed with upstream before the fix and agrees after it, and the reading is 12 -> 0 rather than 13 -> 1. Measured twice — once as a throwaway experiment at 0a.1 with the raw un-gate, once here with the block_offset amendment included.

THREE OF THE TWELVE MOVED TO AN UPSTREAM ANSWER THAT IS ITSELF WRONG, and that is deliberate rather than overlooked. A code span opening with a line ending now reports 1:3..3:0 on both sides: a start one past the end of a two-byte line, and an end naming column zero. This gate is satisfied because it asks whether an outside authority agrees; specs/positions/places.json is the one that asks whether a coordinate names a byte, and it carries those three rows.

Only Code and HTML are compared, because upstream carries this repository's autolink, link-start, emphasis-start and consumed-definition position defects too: widening the comparison would make it go red on the commits that fix them. 0a.6 is the proof — it fixed the autolink column defect in the same commit, and upstream still reports the old numbers.
